styles.label: Culture
styles.blurb: Museums, festivals and the Plateau's street art.

styles.label: Food
styles.blurb: Bagels, smoked meat, markets and BYOB bistros.

styles.label: History
styles.blurb: Old Montreal's cobbled lanes, basilica and waterfront.

stays.why: Central for shopping, museums and the main metro lines; easy walk to the Plateau and Old Montreal.
Cobbled streets, the basilica and the waterfront on your doorstep; prettiest at night.
Cheaper, lively and full of cafés and BYOB restaurants; walk up to Mount Royal park.
Next to the main festival venues and a short walk from both Downtown and Old Montreal.

food: Try the local classics: a Montreal bagel (chewier and sweeter than New York's), smoked meat sandwiches, and poutine.
Jean-Talon Market in Little Italy is great for cheese, produce and cheap snacks; Atwater Market is closer to Downtown.
Many small restaurants in the Plateau are BYOB — bring your own wine from a corner store (dépanneur) to save money.
Brunch is a local ritual; expect queues on weekend mornings, so go early or book ahead.
Prices vary widely: a casual lunch is roughly $12–20, dinner mains around $20–35. Check menus on the day.
more_time: Add a half-day on Mount Royal: walk up from the Plateau for city views, or take bus 11 to the lookout.
Cross to the south shore for a different view: check river shuttles in summer, or take the metro to Parc Jean-Drapeau.
Rainy day? Swap a walk for the Museum of Fine Arts or the McCord Stewart Museum; check opening hours on the day.

recommend.why: Two nights covers Old Montreal, the Plateau and a Mount Royal walk; add a night for museums and a day trip.

month_notes: January: coldest month, highs around -6°C. Dress in layers and plan indoor sights.
February: still deep winter, highs near -4°C. Good for museums and cafés.
March: slowly warming to about 2°C, but nights stay below freezing. Expect slush.
April: mild days near 9°C with cold nights. Pack a rain jacket.
May: pleasant at around 18°C. A great month for walking and terraces.
June: warm, highs near 22°C, but one of the wetter months. Carry an umbrella.
July: the hottest month, highs around 25°C. Festival season; book ahead.
August: warm and humid, highs near 24°C. Busy with summer visitors.
September: comfortable at about 20°C and drier. One of the best months to visit.
October: cool at around 13°C with autumn colours. Bring a warm layer.
November: cold, highs near 5°C, and wet. Fewer crowds.
December: winter returns, highs around -1°C. Festive lights in Old Montreal.

climate_guide.summary: Humid continental climate: long cold winters, warm humid summers, and rain in every month.

items.title: Best time: June to September
items.text: Warm days around 20–25°C. Ideal for walking, parks and festivals.

items.title: Winter is long and cold
items.text: December to March highs sit between -6°C and 2°C, with nights well below freezing. Pack a heavy coat, hat and gloves.

items.title: Rain all year
items.text: Expect roughly 9–14 wet days every month. A compact umbrella is worth carrying.

items.title: Humid summers
items.text: July and August feel muggy, highs near 24–25°C. Plan outdoor time for mornings.

items.title: Shoulder seasons are mild
items.text: May and September–October are comfortable, around 13–20°C, with fewer crowds.

items.title: What to pack
items.text: Layers for changing weather, a waterproof jacket, comfortable walking shoes, and warm winter gear if visiting December to March.

transit.best: The metro for most trips; walk in the Plateau and Old Montreal.

modes.text: 4 lines, frequent and fast. $3.50 per ride or a $10 day pass.
Extensive network; use the same tickets as the metro.
Taxis are available but pricier; Uber and Lyft operate.
Traffic and parking are challenging; not recommended for short visits.
Great for the Plateau and Old Montreal. BIXI bike-share costs $5 for 24h access, with many bike lanes.
No tourist ferry, but river shuttles run in summer.
